text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- A group of right wing parties united in the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) has threatened AWS leader Marian Krzaklewski to leave AWS if he does not give up the idea of fusing all AWS political groupings into one party.

- Sweden is considering purchasing Sokol helicopters made by the PZL Swidnik plant. Proceeds from the Sokol choppers could partly pay for the Jas 39 Gripen multipurpose fighter aircraft if Poland chooses to buy them.
- The concordat treaty between Poland and the Vatican is in agreement with Polish law and should be ratified, Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland will apply in October for membership in the international Union for the Coordination of Electricity Generation and Transmission (UCPTE), national power grid (PSE) deputy strategy director Malgorzata Plucinska-Klawe said.
- Poland's inflation rate fell below 15 percent in May and the government may revise down the annual inflation forecast, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.
- The U.S.'s Texaco Inc. will invest $500 million in construction of 300 petrol stations in the next 10 years, Texaco Poland director Peter Oakford said.
- Poland is now Europe's biggest market for new technologies, machinery and equipment, Finance Minister Belka said in an opening address at the Poznan international fair.
- The Centrum Leasingu i Finansow (CLiF) leasing firm wants to lease passenger cars on the same conditions as other vehicles, CLiF deputy president Dariusz Baran said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Export sales of the listed Vistula SA garment maker made up 32 percent of the firm's output in 1996, showing a slight 1.8 percent decline compared with year before, Vistula spokesman Dariusz Tabaka said.
- Poland's average milk prices increased by 6.6 percent in the first five months of 1997 compared with average prices in 1996, a survey by the PISiPAR agricultural market research institute said.
- More than 200 vehicles were exhibited at the Auto Tour Market Poland international fair in Wroclaw, southwestern Poland last week.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's butter consumption grew by 8.0 percent in 1996 compared with the year before, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The KGHM copper conglomerate will pay out 30 percent of 1997 net profit in dividends to attract investors, KGHM said.
- Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy (BDK) in Lublin, eastern Poland, has provided consumer and motor car credits worth 2.6 billion zlotys since the beginning of the year, the bank said.
ZYCIE

- Life insurance premiums grew by 50.2 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the previous quarter, a survey by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. Non-life premiums grew by 40.9 percent and the sector's combined premium revenues were 4.135 billion zlotys in the period.
- The KGHM copper conglomerate will invest $850 million in development and environment protection schemes by 2001, the firm said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
